body_content:
Ryan,

This is the third time I'm reaching out about the p95 latency degradation we've been seeing on the streaming inference endpoint since Aug 18. I still haven't had a substantive reply on the initial report or on my Sep 8 follow-up with Grafana captures.

Here's where we are:

1. Aug 18: reported sustained p95 above 1200ms during our 09:00 to 11:00 UTC traffic peak. Contractual target under our MSA is p95 at or below 800ms.

Our platform team needs a written response from FeedFlux before end of day Wednesday (Sep 23). Specifically:

1. A root-cause statement, even a preliminary one.
2. Whether you're treating this as an SLA breach for September under our MSA.
3. A mitigation timeline you're willing to put in writing.

Can we grab 30 min Wednesday morning? 10:30 to 11:00 PT works my end. I'd rather solve this at the engineering-to-engineering level before I take it to our VP Eng.

Marcus

subject: v2.4 customer feedback: need your read before Friday
body_preview: Hi Ryan, I ran design-partner check-ins last week ahead of the v2.4 launch. Feedback is mostly positive, but two themes came up that I want your read on before
body_content:
Hi Ryan,

I ran design-partner check-ins last week ahead of the v2.4 launch. Feedback is mostly positive, but two themes came up that I want your read on before the launch review on Wednesday.

First, the migration story from v2.3 checkpoint format. Three of five customers asked whether existing thread state auto-migrates or if they need to run a manual step. From what I remember of David's design doc, we're doing lazy migration on first read. Is that still the plan? And should we call it out explicitly in the release notes, or leave it to the migration guide?

Second, the latency envelope. Two customers (including Kestrel, which I know you're already in the weeds on) asked whether v2.4's new checkpoint path changes the p95 they should expect. If we have a defensible answer here, even 'no material change', it would help.

I don't need essays on either. A couple of sentences per point is enough for me to draft the release notes and prep the review deck. Can you get me something before Friday morning?

Also happy to sit in on the Kestrel response if a fresh set of eyes on the customer-facing wording helps.

Chloe

subject: RFC: migrating durable checkpoint from SQLite to Postgres
body_preview: Hi Ryan, Attached is the first draft of the RFC on moving the durable checkpoint store from SQLite (single-file, single-process) to Postgres (shared,
body_content:
Hi Ryan,

Attached is the first draft of the RFC on moving the durable checkpoint store from SQLite (single-file, single-process) to Postgres (shared, multi-instance-ready). It's not blocking v2.4. That's staying on SQLite. This is Q4 scoping, so we can talk about it after launch.

High-level points I want your read on:

First, the proposal is to keep SQLite as the default for local dev and single-process deployments, and gate the Postgres backend behind a config flag. I do not want to force Postgres onto users who don't need it. Curious if you think that split adds enough operational complexity to be a bad idea.

Second, the lazy migration story from SQLite to Postgres for existing thread state is more painful than I first thought. I've proposed a one-time export tool rather than a runtime shim. Would appreciate your take.

Third, I've explicitly deferred distributed locking, leader election, and cross-instance coordination out of scope. This RFC is 'multi-instance-capable', not 'multi-instance-coordinating'. Want to make sure you're OK with that framing before I circulate more widely.

I'm not asking you to LGTM the whole thing this week. Just want early signal on those three before I bring it to Priya. Aiming to have a version ready to discuss at the Runtime Deep-Dive on Oct 1.

David

subject: PR review request: rate limiter refactor (#492)
body_preview: Hi Ryan, Thanks again for the pointers at last week's 1:1. I reworked the token-bucket rate limiter as we discussed: 1. Split the sync and async paths into two
body_content:
Hi Ryan,

Thanks again for the pointers at last week's 1:1. I reworked the token-bucket rate limiter as we discussed:

1. Split the sync and async paths into two implementations behind a common interface, rather than the ternary-heavy hybrid I had before.
2. Moved the bucket state into a small dataclass instead of the four separate instance attributes.
3. Added the pathological test case you mentioned (rapid successive refills while a burst is in flight).

PR: https://code.feedflux.co/runtime/pull/492

Couple of things I'd especially like your read on. First, I kept the async lock even for the sync path. It's technically unnecessary but avoids a class hierarchy split. Curious whether you'd take the class split instead. Second, the refill jitter is currently a hardcoded 5%. I don't have a strong reason for that number. Open to changing it or making it configurable.

No rush, but if you can get to it before end of week that'd be great. Priya is looking at it too. I'll incorporate both rounds together.

Thanks,
Jamie

subject: Post-mortem: edge provider outage on Sep 9, impact on our us-west traffic
body_preview: Attaching the internal write-up on the Sep 9 edge provider outage that hit our us-west traffic between 09:12 and 10:47 UTC. What happened: our upstream edge
body_content:
Attaching the internal write-up on the Sep 9 edge provider outage that hit our us-west traffic between 09:12 and 10:47 UTC.

What happened: our upstream edge provider pushed a routing policy change that interacted incorrectly with a rate-limit rule set they'd updated 20 minutes earlier. Result: about 1h 35min of elevated 503 rates on requests routed through us-west and us-central. Their post-incident report is attached.

What we saw:

1. Elevated error rate on the streaming endpoint for the affected window.
2. Our cache and static asset paths were unaffected.
3. Retries at our layer masked most of the impact for customers, but tail latency was noticeably worse.

What we're doing:

1. No code change on our side. Root cause was upstream.
2. Adding an internal runbook entry so on-call knows what to look for if we see this signature again.
3. Following up with our account team on their commitment to region-staged rollouts by Q4.

No action required. Post-mortem is attached for anyone who wants the full timeline.

Ryan,

Following up on my Aug 18 email about p95 latency on the streaming endpoint. We've now seen the same pattern six times over the last three weeks, and I haven't had a response.

Attached is a set of Grafana screenshots covering the six occurrences (Aug 18, Aug 25, Sep 1, Sep 4, Sep 6, and this morning). Each one is a sustained spike starting around 09:00 UTC and lasting 45 to 90 minutes. p95 in the affected window is between 1150 and 1380ms. Our MSA target is 800ms.

No action required unless you see a problem. Loop me in if you do.

Sarah

subject: Runtime Deep-Dive #7: Checkpoint migration path (Thu Oct 1, noon PT)
body_preview: Hi team, Next Runtime Deep-Dive is on Thu Oct 1, 12:00 to 13:00 PT. I'll be presenting. Topic: what a durable checkpoint migration from SQLite to Postgres
body_content:
Hi team,

Next Runtime Deep-Dive is on Thu Oct 1, 12:00 to 13:00 PT. I'll be presenting.

Topic: what a durable checkpoint migration from SQLite to Postgres actually costs you. I'll walk through the RFC I've been circulating and get into the parts I've been going back and forth on. Specifically the migration story for existing thread state, and the boundary between 'multi-instance-capable' and 'multi-instance-coordinating'.

Who this is for:

1. Anyone who might end up touching the durable checkpoint store in Q4 or Q1.
2. Anyone thinking about the operational side of running us in production.
3. Anyone who just wants to argue about database migrations for an hour.

Format: 25 min presentation, 25 min structured discussion, 10 min open Q&A. Deck goes up 24 hours ahead so async folks can read before the live session.

Recording will be posted afterwards for people who can't make it. RSVP not required. Drop by if the topic is useful.

David

P.S. If you want to see the current draft of the RFC ahead of the session, ping me directly.

subject: Weekly Platform Guild, Thu: durable checkpoint patterns (Ryan hosting)
body_preview: Weekly Platform Guild is this Thursday, Sep 17, 15:00 to 16:00 PT. Topic: durable checkpoint patterns across LangGraph, temporal.io, and Restate Host: Ryan
body_content:
Weekly Platform Guild is this Thursday, Sep 17, 15:00 to 16:00 PT.

Topic: durable checkpoint patterns across LangGraph, temporal.io, and Restate
Host: Ryan

What to expect: a structured comparison of how three different durable-execution frameworks handle checkpoint state, recovery from mid-execution failures, and re-entrant semantics. Not a 'which is best' exercise. The point is to sharpen the vocabulary we use internally when we describe our own choices in v2.4 and the Q4 Postgres RFC.

Structure:

1. 10 min. What 'durable checkpoint' even means and why the terminology varies.
2. 30 min. Framework-by-framework walkthrough with runnable examples.
3. 20 min. Open discussion. Where does our current SQLite approach sit on the same axes?

Prep material (optional):

1. Two design docs in the guild folder, marked 'read before Thursday'.
2. LangGraph checkpointer source: docs link in the invite.

Zoom link and shared doc in the calendar invite. Recording as usual.

Platform Guild

subject: p95 latency degradation in prod, need root cause
body_preview: Hi Ryan, We've been seeing sustained p95 latency above 1200ms on the streaming inference endpoint during our morning traffic peak (09:00 to 11:00 UTC). Our MSA
body_content:
Hi Ryan,

We've been seeing sustained p95 latency above 1200ms on the streaming inference endpoint during our morning traffic peak (09:00 to 11:00 UTC). Our MSA target is p95 at or below 800ms, so this is meaningfully outside our expected envelope.

What we know so far:

1. Started at some point between our last measurement on Aug 15 and this morning.
2. Isolated to the morning traffic peak. Off-peak p95 is well within target.
3. Same endpoint, same model provider, same request shape as our baseline load tests. No client-side change on our end that would explain it.
4. Sample of about 30 affected request IDs pulled from our logs, happy to share.

Could someone on your side take a look and let us know what you're seeing? If this is related to a rollout on your end, understanding the timeline would help us plan around it.

This is not (yet) an SLA question. Just want to understand what's happening before it becomes one.

Thanks,
Marcus

Senior Platform Engineer, Kestrel Payments

subject: Platform Engineering Summit 2027, would love a submission from FeedFlux
body_preview: Hi Ryan, I'm on the program committee for Platform Engineering Summit 2027 (Feb 24 to 25, in San Francisco). CFP is open through Oct 31. We came across your
body_content:
Hi Ryan,

I'm on the program committee for Platform Engineering Summit 2027 (Feb 24 to 25, in San Francisco). CFP is open through Oct 31.

We came across your team's runtime reliability write-up and thought it would make a strong 30-minute talk. The parts we found most compelling were the deterministic fault-injection harness, the framing of transient vs. terminal error classes, and how you validated the idempotency ledger without paying real provider costs. That intersection of 'agents' and 'boring reliability engineering' is exactly the kind of content we want on the platform track.

If you'd consider submitting, we can help polish an abstract and we do formal talk coaching for accepted speakers. Two speaker slots are open on the platform track. Talks are 30 minutes plus 10 for Q&A.

If FeedFlux isn't the right fit this year but you know someone doing similar work at another company, please forward. We're actively looking for talks in this space.

Details and submission link: https://platformsummit.org/2027/cfp

Thanks for considering,
Priya Iyer
Program Committee, Platform Engineering Summit
